text:
Mei: morning micro-disaster  spilled my double-shot americano straight into the power strip and the little travel switch i keep under the desk. laptop lived but ethernet died. send help. :coffee::sob:
Connor: yikes. immediate step: unplug the strip from mains, pull laptop battery if removable, dry everything, and don't plug back in for a bit. also post a pic if you want lol.
Mei: unplugged, drying with towel and a fan. pic: /files/espresso_mayhem.jpg. ethernet port on the switch shows amber and then nothing.
Priya: if the switch died, you can bypass with a laptop USB-C ethernet dongle until replacement. also check the wall jack to ensure cable is fine.
Liam: check `ip a` and `sudo ethtool eth0` to see if link shows at all. if the RJ45 looks toasted, try a different patch cable.
Mei: `ip a` shows only loopback and wlan0. no eth. `dmesg | tail` shows `usb 1-2: new high-speed USB device` and some USB errors from the powered hub.
Connor: sounds like the powered hub/switch is the casualty. if you need to jump on a call now, hotspot + tether is fastest. I have a spare gigabit switch in my trunk if you want me to drop it off (i'm 10 mins away).
Priya: PSA: keep backups of tiny networking bits in a drawer. i have 2 spare dongles and a switch. also file an expense for replacement under Home Office Equipment.
Liam: be careful about plugging things back in too soon. condensation can cause shorts. give it an hour at least with good airflow.
Mei: thanks y'all. will use hotspot for standup. Connor if you can swing by that would be awesome 60a
status-bot: reminder: "Home office equipment" reimbursement available. See handbook: https://intranet.example/expenses/home-office
Connor: happy to drop by. also suggest moving the espresso maker off the desk. mine used to live on the bookshelf and tipped once 4a6
Mei: lesson learned. moving coffee to a dedicated tray on the counter immediately. also ordering a small surge-protected switch and a sleeve for cables. any brand recs?
Priya: Netgear/TP-Link basic unmanaged switches are fine. for dongles, Anker or Cable Matters tend to be reliable.
Liam: if you want rugged: industrial metal-cased switch but higher cost. for home, no need.
Mei: ok ordering Netgear 5-port and an Anker dongle. will ping receipts. thanks for the rescue offers and tips. ETA for drying: 45m.
Connor: cool. ping when you're back online and i'll swing by with the spare switch if you want to keep the new one pristine.
Mei: will do. and yes, zero coffee near cables from now on :raised_hands:
